CREATOR_STORY.TITLE: The Story Behind Locker
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P1: I have been a passionate blockchain builder since 2015, involved in numerous projects over the years. Eventually, I withdrew from public endeavors for the security of myself and my family.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P2: However, despite being highly security-conscious, I was hacked. My wallets were drained. That harsh reality taught me a critical lesson: hardware wallets alone are not enough if the machine you interact with is corrupted.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P3: Driven by this, I spent nearly 2 years architecting and developing this end-to-end secure ecosystem. By isolating the keystore physically (Air-gap) and verifying exact transaction payloads, it ensures that even on a fully compromised computer, hackers cannot steal your funds.
CREATOR_STORY.CONTENT_P4: Today, I am opening this architecture to the community. Everything is 100% open-source, so you never have to experience what I went through.

FAQ.TITLE: Comprehensive Knowledge Base
FAQ.Q1: What exactly is the Locker Protocol?
FAQ.A1: The Locker Protocol is a highly secure, non-custodial smart contract suite designed to lock, vest, and manage ERC-20 tokens. Instead of relying on a single private key or a centralized entity, it allows anyone to deploy their own private, isolated instances governed by multi-signature M-of-N mechanics. It includes advanced features like time locks, price-based target locks (via Uniswap Oracles), and batch operations, all fully orchestrated by immutable smart contracts on-chain.
FAQ.Q2: Why is this system fundamentally safer than standard multi-signature wallets (like Safe)?
FAQ.A2: Traditional hardware wallets and multisigs still require you to connect your signing device (via USB, Bluetooth, or software bridging) to an internet-connected computer. If that computer is severely compromised by malware, it might silently alter the transaction payload before you sign it. The Locker Protocol prevents this entirely by using a true Air-Gapped architecture. Payloads are exchanged visually via animated QR codes between the online Manager App and an offline Tablet App. You mathematically verify the exact action on the completely isolated device before signing, preventing any man-in-the-middle attacks.
FAQ.Q3: How does the Air-Gapped Wallet app actually work in practice?
FAQ.A3: The Air-Gapped Wallet is a Progressive Web Application (PWA). You navigate to the repository on a dedicated device (like an old smartphone or tablet) while connected to the internet, install it to your device's home screen, and then permanently disconnect that device (Airplane Mode, forget WiFi networks). From that day forward, the offline device securely generates your private keys and seed phrases locally. It communicates with the online world strictly by scanning and generating QR codes using your device's camera.
FAQ.Q4: Do I really need a dedicated, permanently offline device?
FAQ.A4: For the absolute highest tier of security, yes. Repurposing an old smartphone, factory resetting it, and never connecting it to the internet guarantees that remote hackers cannot extract your private keys, regardless of zero-day exploits. However, for testing or lower-stakes environments, you can run the Air-Gapped Wallet app on your primary machine. But the true power of the architecture is realized when physical isolation (the air-gap) is strictly maintained.
FAQ.Q5: I am not a developer or highly technical person. Can I still use this?
FAQ.A5: Absolutely. The complexity of compiling Solidity code, verifying contracts, and linking libraries is completely abstracted away by the '1-Click UI Deployment'. Any user can select their parameters, pay the one-time deployment fee, and the Manager App will sequentially deploy incredibly complex smart contract hierarchies in the background. Once deployed, managing your locker through the interface is designed to be as intuitive as standard banking applications.
FAQ.Q6: What happens if I lose access to the online device (Manager App) or if the website goes down?
FAQ.A6: The Manager App is merely a convenient interface to interact with the blockchain. It holds zero funds and zero private keys. If you lose your computer, or if our hosted user interface disappears, your funds remain 100% secure on the blockchain. Because the entire ecosystem is open-source, you can download the Manager App code from GitHub, run it locally on any computer globally, point it to your deployed contract address, and regain full access to your Locker instantly.
FAQ.Q7: What happens if my offline device (Tablet App) is destroyed, lost, or broken?
FAQ.A7: When you generate a new wallet within the offline Air-Gapped App, you will be provided with a standard 12 or 24-word recovery phrase (BIP-39 mnemonic). You must write this phrase down on paper or stamp it into metal and store it in a physical safe. If your offline device breaks, simply install the Air-Gapped Wallet on a new offline device, click 'Import Seed Phrase', enter your physical backup, and all your keys and access rights will be perfectly restored. No assets are lost.
FAQ.Q8: Can we change the signers (add or remove people) after the Locker is deployed?
FAQ.A8: Yes. The protocol features a flexible `SignerManager` contract. Operations such as 'Add Signer', 'Remove Signer', or 'Change Security Threshold' can be proposed at any time. However, to execute these administrative changes, the current active signers must cryptographically approve the request. This means no rogue administrator or founder can unilaterally add themselves or remove others without reaching the strictly enforced multi-signature quorum.
FAQ.Q9: How do Multi-Signature Thresholds (M-of-N) work in detail?
FAQ.A9: When deploying or updating your Locker, you set two parameters: the total number of authorized signers (N) and the minimum number of approvals needed to execute an action (M). For example, a 3-of-5 threshold means you register 5 trusted people (partners, lawyers, cold storage devices). To withdraw funds or alter settings, at least 3 distinct signers must sequentially scan the request and provide valid cryptographic QR signatures. The smart contract mathematically verifies all 3 unique EIP-712 signatures before allowing execution.
FAQ.Q10: What is 'Gasless Execution' and who actually pays the blockchain network fees?
FAQ.A10: In standard systems, every signer must submit their own transaction and pay ETH (gas), requiring every signer to maintain a funded hot wallet. In the Locker Protocol, signers only generate off-chain cryptographic signatures via their offline tablets and pass the QR codes back to the Manager. Once you've collected the required threshold of signatures, ANY wallet (even one that is not an authorized signer) can act as the 'relayer'. The relayer submits the bundle of signatures as a single transaction and pays the gas fee once. The contract unpacks the bundle and executes the action.
FAQ.Q11: Are my private keys or seed phrases ever transmitted via Bluetooth, NFC, or USB?
FAQ.A11: Never. The Air-Gapped Wallet does not use Bluetooth, NFC, WiFi, cellular data, or USB cables to communicate with the Manager App. The sole transmission medium is visual light—scanning animated QR codes (using the BC-UR Keystone protocol). This guarantees that malicious software on the online computer cannot 'cross the gap' via hidden network protocols or infected USB buses to steal your seed phrase.
FAQ.Q12: How does the 'Price Target Unlocking' feature function under the hood?
FAQ.A12: Aside from generic time-based vesting (e.g., locking tokens until January 1st, 2026), the Locker Protocol integrates directly with Uniswap V2 and V3 On-Chain Oracles. You can configure a lock that says 'Unlock these 100,000 arbitrary tokens ONLY if their market price reaches $5.00 USD'. The smart contract dynamically queries the live liquidity pools to verify the asset's value in real-time. If the targeted upside or downside threshold is met, the contract mathematically permits the withdrawal without manual intervention.
FAQ.Q13: A user mistakenly sent random tokens directly to the contract address. Are they lost forever?
FAQ.A13: In many basic smart contracts, accidentally transferred tokens are permanently burned or stuck. The Locker Protocol includes a 'Token Rescue' mechanism. The authorized multi-signature owners can generate a Rescue Payload for any specific ERC-20 token address. If the threshold approves it, the contract will sweep those loose tokens and return them to the designated owner wallet, effectively saving the assets in emergencies.
FAQ.Q14: Can you explain the $199 fee for the '1-Click UI Deployment'?
FAQ.A14: The $199 fee is a strict, one-time payment required only if you use our automated interface to deploy the complex hierarchy of 6 interlinked smart contracts via the `DeploymentRegistry`. This fee funds the continued development, security auditing, and hosting of the frontend ecosystem. Once the single payment is processed and the contracts are live on the blockchain, you own them unconditionally. We never touch your locked assets.
FAQ.Q15: Are there any hidden recurring subscription fees, or does the protocol take a percentage of locked tokens?
FAQ.A15: No. There are absolutely no hidden costs, no monthly subscriptions, and no percentage cuts taken from your locked assets. Once deployed (either manually or via the UI), your interactions with the smart contracts are strictly peer-to-peer on the blockchain. The protocol does not tax your deposits or withdrawals. The only recurring costs you will ever face are the standard, unavoidable base gas fees charged by the Ethereum or L2 networks for processing transactions.
FAQ.Q16: Can developers truly deploy the contracts entirely for free?
FAQ.A16: Yes. Because the entire smart contract suite is fully open-source on GitHub, technical users can clone the repository, compile the Solidity code locally using Hardhat or Foundry, and deploy the contracts manually to the blockchain. By bypassing the central `DeploymentRegistry`, you avoid the $199 convenience fee entirely. After manual deployment, you can inject your contract addresses into the open-source frontend and use the entire UI completely free of charge.
FAQ.Q17: Does the Locker Protocol rely on a centralized backend server or database?
FAQ.A17: No. There are no proprietary backend APIs, databases (like SQL or MongoDB), or centralized corporate servers managing your state. The entire state of your locks, signers, vesting schedules, and thresholds is stored immutably on the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). The Angular web interface connects directly and exclusively to RPC nodes via MetaMask. If our web hosting fails, the protocol continues to function perfectly.
FAQ.Q18: How does the 'Batch Management' feature save time and network fees?
FAQ.A18: Interacting with smart contracts individually can be expensive and tedious. When you need to lock tokens for 50 different team members or investors, sending 50 separate transactions would be costly in gas. Our Batch Management interface allows you to compile an array of multiple locks, recipients, timings, and token amounts into a single massive payload. Your signers approve the single batch payload via QR, and one execution transaction processes all 50 operations simultaneously, saving significant gas.
FAQ.Q19: Which blockchain networks do you officially support?
FAQ.A19: The Locker Protocol is fully EVM-compatible and is designed to run natively on the most robust networks. We currently officially support Ethereum Mainnet for peak security, alongside major Layer-2 scaling solutions and high-throughput chains including Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Smart Chain, Linea, and zkSync Era. Configuration for all these networks is pre-built into the frontend routing logic.
FAQ.Q20: Is the codebase open to the public for review, and has it been audited?
FAQ.A20: Total transparency is our core tenet. The entire architecture—every line of Solidity in the smart contracts, every TypeScript file in the Manager App, and every cryptographic routine in the offline Air-Gapped Wallet—is 100% open-source and publicly hosted on GitHub. We invite and encourage developers, security researchers, and hackers to inspect, fork, and verify the integrity of the ecosystem. True trust is mathematically verifiable, not promised.
